beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Last question of the war: how does it end — for everyone? The billions who never heard. The babies. If God is who this film says He is, the ending has to be worthy of Him. It is.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The devil's deadline was death — die unreached, lose forever. God refuses that math. Everyone goes first to the spirit world, where the dead are TAUGHT. In nineteen eighteen, a prophet was shown the machinery:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: From among the righteous, he organized his forces and appointed messengers, clothed with power and authority, and commissioned them to go forth and carry the light of the gospel to them that were in darkness, even unto all the spirits of men.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And I also beheld that all children who die before they arrive at the years of accountability are saved in the celestial kingdom of heaven.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: All children. Highest heaven. No exceptions. If you have lost a little one — that is where they are. And that is who God is.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Then the judgment itself. In eighteen thirty-two, the vision of the end was opened to Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon — and the first thing they wrote down was not thrones. It was Him:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: And now, after the many testimonies which have been given of him, this is the testimony, last of all, which we give of him: That he lives! For we saw him, even on the right hand of God; and we heard the voice bearing record that he is the Only Begotten of the Father.

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for one star differeth from another star in glory.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Celestial. Terrestrial. Telestial. Sun, moon, and stars — even the least a glory beyond understanding. The ending agency requires: everyone receives what they truly chose. Not an incinerator. A homecoming.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Is hell real? Yes — as anguish before judgment. Outer darkness waits only for the few who gain full knowledge and choose full rebellion. For every other darkness there is a door out — and Christ holds it open.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Add up the ending. Every child, safe. Every never-reached soul, reached. Resurrection, free, for all. Kingdoms, not a furnace. Now say the article of faith with me:

beats.speaker: scripture
beats.text: We believe that through the Atonement of Christ, all mankind may be saved, by obedience to the laws and ordinances of the Gospel.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: All mankind may be saved. That is the most generous account of God's justice ever revealed — and the only ending that matches the Father you have watched: the one who wept with Enoch, and paid the whole bill in a garden. Vengeance was never the plan. Family was.

card.speaker: narrator
card.text: Heaven is not a gated community. It is a Father losing as close to nobody as agency allows.
